sources.title: D. Tong, Classical Dynamics (Cambridge lecture notes, January 2015 printing), 139 PDF pages
sources.locator: Chapter 1: Section 1.2 printed pages 2-5 (PDF pages 8-11) and Section 1.3 printed pages 5-9 (PDF pages 11-15)

contents.name: Section 1.3 Eqs. (1.11)-(1.16): the force decomposition F_i = sum_j F_ij + F_i^ext, the third law, total mass M, centre of mass R, Pdot = F^ext and M Rddot = F^ext
Section 1.3 Eqs. (1.17)-(1.19): Ldot as the external torque plus the pair sum (r_i - r_j) x F_ij and the parallelism (centrality) condition
Section 1.3 Eqs. (1.22)-(1.23): r_i = R + rtilde_i and the kinetic-energy split T = (1/2) M Rdot^2 + (1/2) sum_i m_i rtilde_i^2
Section 1.3.2 Eqs. (1.24)-(1.25): the work integrals of the external and internal forces, conservative external and internal potentials, and conservation of H = T + V
Section 1.2: the ten transformations relating inertial frames (rotations, translations, boosts and time translation)
Section 1.3.1: the Lorentz-force example and the momentum carried by the electromagnetic field as the resolution of the apparent third-law failure
contents.reason: Field momentum belongs to the classical-electromagnetism framework and is not imported here; this page records the third-law caution without it in rem-cm03-conservation-scope.

contents.name: Section 2 onward: Lagrangian and variational formalism, normal modes, rigid bodies
contents.reason: The Lagrangian and variational development belongs to the CM07-CM13 pages of the track; this page stays in the Newtonian force branch.

sources.title: D. Tong, Dynamics and Relativity (Cambridge lecture notes, Lent 2013), 166 PDF pages

contents.name: Section 1.2.1: boosts x' = x + v t map inertial frames to inertial frames and preserve d^2x/dt^2 = 0, with the velocity transformation adding the boost velocity

sources.title: K. K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics, Part CM: Classical Mechanics (title page last edited September 1, 2026)
sources.locator: Section 1.1 point (v), chapter pages 2-3 (PDF pages 6-7); Section 1.3, chapter pages 6-10 (PDF pages 10-14); Section 1.4, chapter pages 10-11 (PDF pages 14-15)

contents.name: Section 1.1 point (v): transfer of the radius vector, velocity and acceleration between frames in relative translation; inertial frames as frames moving without rotation
Section 1.3 Eqs. (1.29)-(1.30): the decomposition F_k = sum F_kk' + F_k^(ext) and Pdot = F^(ext) after internal cancellation, in an inertial frame
Section 1.3 Eqs. (1.31)-(1.38): L = r x p, Ldot = tau, the total angular momentum of a system and the cancellation of internal torque pairs for central mutual forces
Section 1.3 Eqs. (1.19)-(1.21): T = m v^2/2, dT = F dot dr and the work-energy principle

Section 1.3 Eqs. (1.22)-(1.27) with footnote 15: potential forces F = -nabla U, the work of potential forces as the difference of U at the endpoints, E = T + U conserved for conservative forces only, and U defined up to an additive constant
Section 1.3 Eqs. (1.25)-(1.27): mechanical energy conservation for conservative forces and the change of E by non-conservative forces

Section 1.3 closing remark: the conservation laws are first integrals of the equations of motion and introduce nothing new dynamically, with the central-force condition for the angular-momentum statement
Section 1.4: potential energy and equilibrium, extrema of U as equilibria and the stability discussion
contents.reason: Equilibrium and stability belong to the one-dimensional and stability pages (CM04, CM16); this page states and proves no equilibrium or stability result.

short_document_reading.completeness_evidence: Complete document read. PDF p.1 opens with the title, contents and Section 1 (Definition 1 star-shaped sets, Proposition 2) and Section 2 through Theorem 3 (equivalent characterisations of conservative C^1 fields). PDF p.2 carries Sections 2.1-2.3 with Proposition 4, Theorem 5 (n=2 Poincare lemma), the punctured-plane vortex counterexample with circulation -2pi, Proposition 6, Proposition 7, Theorem 8 (n=3) and Theorem 11 (general n). PDF p.3 carries Section 3 (Proposition 13, Theorem 14, Proposition 15 radial-primitive formula for the vector potential) and Section 4 (Theorem 16, the de Rham formulation), which is the last line; the document ends there with no truncation marker.
